findings.title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently breaks the 4-argument form
findings.body: `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is defined at line 145 and then immediately redefined at line 149 as `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the second definition wins, so the width/height variant is unreachable. Any existing caller doing `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, w, h)` (or with opts) now binds `h` to `dimensions` and the opts hash/height to `opts`, producing either a bogus `-resize` argument or a `TypeError` when `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` is evaluated on an Integer. Use a single method that accepts either a dimension string or width/height instead of two same-named methods.

findings.title: Client upload size limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
findings.body: `maxSizeKB` was read from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024`. Sites that configure a smaller limit will let users upload files the server will reject (bad UX, wasted bandwidth), and sites configured above 10MB will see valid uploads blocked client-side. The error message also now always says 10240 kb regardless of the actual configured limit. This looks like leftover debug code (PR description is "Test 1") and should read the setting again.

findings.title: 413 error message hardcodes 10MB instead of configured max image size
findings.body: In `displayErrorForUpload`, the 413 branch no longer uses `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` and instead reports `10 * 1024` kb. The user is therefore told a limit that may have nothing to do with the real configured/web-server limit, which is misleading.

findings.title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB instead of the site setting
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. Administrators can no longer restrict the amount of remote data an API upload will pull down; a site configured for e.g. 1MB images now fetches up to 10MB per request (resource/DoS exposure), and sites configured above 10MB silently lose functionality. Derive the cap from the setting.

findings.title: Downsize loop uses a possibly stale `tempfile.size` and converts a file in place while its handle is open
findings.body: The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` (source == destination) and then re-reads `tempfile.size`. `Tempfile#size` stats the still-open file descriptor; ImageMagick/ImageOptim may replace the file (new inode) rather than truncate it in place, in which case the loop keeps seeing the original size, burns all 5 attempts re-shrinking the image, and then passes a wrong filesize to `Upload.create_for`. Re-open/stat the path (e.g. `File.size(tempfile.path)`) after each conversion and pass that size to `create_for`.

findings.title: Percentage dimension and extension-less temp path break animated GIF handling
findings.body: `downsize` is called with the dimension string `"80%"`. For animated images `OptimizedImage.optimize` would dispatch to the gifsicle path, but (a) that branch only triggers when the source path matches `/\.GIF$/i` and the upload tempfile has no `.gif` extension, so it never triggers, and (b) gifsicle's `--resize-fit` does not accept a percentage (`--scale` is the percentage option), so it would fail if it did. Consequently large animated GIFs are run through `convert #{from}[0]`, which keeps only the first frame and silently destroys the animation.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores conversion failure
findings.body: The return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is discarded. `convert_with` returns false (and only logs) when ImageMagick or ImageOptim fails, so on failure the loop spins through all 5 attempts invoking an external process each time with no effect, before creating an upload that will be rejected for size. Break out of the loop when the downsize returns false.

findings.title: No tests for the new downsize API or auto-downsizing path
findings.body: The change alters the public signature of `OptimizedImage.optimize`/`downsize` (dimension string instead of width/height), removes `self.dimensions`, and adds a new auto-downsize loop in `UploadsController#create_upload`, but no specs are added or updated. Existing specs that stub/call `optimize(op, from, to, width, height, opts)` or `dimensions` would break, and the new loop (including the size-reread and failure behaviour) is untested.
